skill.name: competitive-ads-extractor
skill.description: Extracts and analyzes competitors' ads from ad libraries (Facebook, LinkedIn, etc.) to understand what messaging, problems, and creative approaches are working. Helps inspire and improve your own ad campaigns.
skill.summary: Research competitor ad libraries and turn public ads into messaging, creative, and campaign insights.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Competitive ad research is slow when teams collect examples manually. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through extraction, categorization, and messaging analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides extraction of public competitor ads from ad libraries.
Organizes ads by theme, audience, format, and message.
Summarizes pain points, value propositions, calls to action, and copy patterns.
Compares messaging across competitors, platforms, or time periods.
Produces research summaries, spreadsheet-ready notes, presentation outlines, and pattern libraries.
limitations: Requires access to public ad libraries or user-provided ad examples.
Cannot prove ad performance unless reliable engagement or spend data is available.
Screenshots and exports depend on platform access, page layout, and permissions.
Users must follow platform terms, privacy rules, and intellectual property obligations.

use_cases.title: Plan Campaign Angles
use_cases.description: Review active competitor ads before drafting new campaign concepts and test angles.

use_cases.title: Map Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare repeated claims, target audiences, and pain points across a competitive set.

use_cases.title: Build Creative References
use_cases.description: Collect examples of formats, layouts, and copy patterns for original creative briefs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Competitor Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with one competitor and one public ad library.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract current public ads for [competitor] from [ad library]. Summarize themes, calls to action, formats, and repeated messages.

prompt_templates.title: Pain Point Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus the review on customer problems and positioning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [competitor] ads about [problem]. Identify pain points, audience segments, value propositions, and copy patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Competitive Set Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare several companies in the same market.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review ads from [company list]. Compare positioning, creative formats, offers, and gaps we can address with original messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Quarterly Trend Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Track how competitor messaging changes over time.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [competitor] ad themes from [period one] and [period two]. Highlight new messages, retired angles, and campaign recommendations.

output_examples.input: Extract current ads from Notion and analyze the strongest messaging themes.
output_examples.output: A report listing active ad counts, top themes, common pain points, creative formats, calls to action, and campaign recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare LinkedIn ads from three B2B project management competitors.
output_examples.output: A comparison of audience focus, positioning claims, proof points, creative patterns, and messaging gaps for each competitor.

output_examples.input: Review video ads and static ads from one competitor.
output_examples.output: A format analysis showing repeated visual structures, headline styles, product proof, and notes on available engagement signals.

best_practices: Use public sources and document the date, platform, and search terms for each extraction.
Look for repeated patterns before turning any single ad into a campaign insight.
Use findings as inspiration for original strategy, copy, and creative direction.
anti_patterns: Do not copy competitor ad copy, designs, or protected creative assets directly.
Do not treat ad frequency as proof of performance without supporting data.
Do not scrape private, restricted, or personal data while collecting ad examples.

faq.question: Which ad libraries can this skill support?
faq.answer: It is written for public ad libraries such as Facebook Ad Library and LinkedIn ad research sources.

faq.question: Does it measure actual ad performance?
faq.answer: It can analyze visible patterns, but it cannot confirm performance without reliable engagement, spend, or conversion data.

faq.question: Can it save screenshots of ads?
faq.answer: Yes, the skill describes saving screenshots when platform access and tool permissions allow it.

faq.question: Is this useful for small marketing teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps small teams structure competitor research before planning original campaigns.

faq.question: How should teams avoid plagiarism?
faq.answer: Use the analysis to identify patterns and gaps, then create new copy, visuals, and offers.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
